title: Count the ninety second cut against Premiere again, once the key gaps close
goal: When the ruler, the keys on open, one-key extract, Q and W and the long-recording freeze are fixed, do the five minute edit again at Next defaults and count every press and drag it takes to reach ninety seconds, so the user knows whether Photonz is now as quick as Premiere at the job it is meant to beat it at. Anything slower than Premiere becomes a task.
notes: Success lines of video-beats-premiere: 'removing a marked stretch is at most three presses' and 'the whole cut to ninety seconds is under 40 presses and drags'. Nothing measures the second one today. The 2026-09-24 digest reflection asks for the Premiere measurement to be re-run after this batch closes rather than filing from guesses. Re-running recipe: 'Re-running this' section of docs/design/video-vs-premiere.md (say + ffmpeg recording, open step). deps: ruler, keys on open, extract/lift, long-recording freeze, Q/W. Probe app only.
acceptance: The five minute talking recording from docs/design/video-vs-premiere.md is cut to about ninety seconds at Next defaults, with no switch turned on, by pressing keys and dragging only
The count of presses and drags is written into docs/design/video-vs-premiere.md beside Premiere's count for the same cut, and it is under 40
Removing one marked stretch is counted separately and is at most three presses (I, O, one key)
Every step slower or clumsier than Premiere is filed as a task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not
The Gaps table in that doc says which of the ten gaps are closed, with a fresh picture for each one that is

log.note: Adversarial pass before counting: the ruler is SwiftUI and a walk's click reaches the canvas, so a ruler click could not be driven; added a clickRuler step that runs the ruler's own gesture (begin/drag/end playhead) at a named moment, without the gesture's snap onto a key. The recording opens paused with the timeline holding the keyboard, so no press was needed before the first cut. Premiere is not installed here, so its count comes from its documented default keys, not a timed run.

Counted: 5:19 to exactly 1:30 in 19 actions (click+Q, 3x click/I/click/O/', click+W); Premiere 20 (same 19 plus making a sequence). One marked stretch = I, O, ' (3 presses). Walk the-ninety-second-cut-walk ok with 4 real captures; longest main-thread hold after a cut key 83 ms; captions 191 -> 58; 8 s playback never blank. Gap walks re-run, all 9 ok with real captures: ruler-names-the-right-time-zoomed, timeline-keys-on-open, extract-a-marked-stretch, a-long-captioned-recording, a-title-reads-over-a-video, ripple-trim-to-playhead, default-transition-key, export-a-video-at-1080p, snapping-switches-with-s.

left rough, did not earn a task: (1) opening Export holds the main thread 310-370 ms in every walk that opens it, on every document from 900x700 stills to 2880x1800 video (35 readings in /tmp/photonz-playtest logs); so constant it looks like the sheet's own presentation being counted as one pass, not a video or size cost, and not confirmed as a freeze a person feels. File it if it shows up as a visible stall. (2) clickRuler does not snap the way a real ruler click does. (3) clickRuler has not been watched under a lock, so the walk is refused on a locked Mac. (4) the first Scripts/test.sh run had 1 failing test I did not capture; the second run was fully green (9686 tests), most likely the tracked export-size flake. Nothing in the cut was slower or clumsier than Premiere, so no follow-up filed.

5:19 cut to exactly 1:30 at Next defaults in 19 actions (ruler clicks + Q, I/O/' x3, W), vs Premiere's 20 from its default keys; under the 40 line; one stretch = 3 presses. New walk the-ninety-second-cut-walk (ok, real captures) with a clickRuler step (parse-tested). docs/design/video-vs-premiere.md has the count and a Now column: gaps 1-9 closed with fresh pictures from their 9 green walks, gap 10 awaits the decision card. Commit fa1f1ea4 (pushed). Tests green.
